newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: New Congo cuts wages in state enterprises.
newsitem.headline: New Congo cuts wages in state enterprises.

text.p: Workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo's state enterprises face temporary wage cuts of between five and 35 percent, national television said on Wednesday.
The television said finance minister Mawapanga Mwana Nanga had gathered workers representatives' at a meeting in the capital Kinshasa to explain the government's decision.
"With the catastrophic economic situation the minister made clear the need for everyone to contribute to a social balance to allow the relaunch of the productive machinery," the television said.

Since taking power last month, the government of President Laurent Kabila has said it is committed to a "social market" economy in Africa's third largest nation -- encouraging private investment but only combined with corporate responsibility.

The state sector is bloated and inefficient after three decades of corruption and mismanagment under ousted President Mobutu Sese Seko, which impoverished the former Zaire in spite of its vast mineral resources.
Among state-run companies are industrial diamond mining company MIBA and copper and cobalt miners GECAMINES, as well as numerous transport companies and utilities.
Mawapanga on Wednesday told a news conference that privatisation of the enterprises was not being considered although efforts were underway to attract private capital.
